artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $B_m(x)$ denote the Bernoulli polynomials, defined by the generating function $\sum_{m\ge 0} B_m(x) t^m/m! = t e^{xt}/(e^t-1)$. For each positive integer $n$, define
$$a_n \;:=\; \frac{1}{n(2n+1)}\binom{2n}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}(5k+1)\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k}(-192)^{\,n-1-k}.$$
Decide the truth of the following three assertions.

(i) For every integer $n\ge 2$, $a_n$ is an integer, except when $2n+1$ is a power of $3$, in which case $3a_n$ is an integer not divisible by $3$.

(ii) For every prime $p>3$ and every positive integer $a$,
$$p^{a}\sum_{k=0}^{p^{a}-1}\frac{(5k+1)}{(-192)^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k} \;\equiv\; \bigl(p^{a}+p^{a-1}\bigr)\,\frac{5}{18}\,p^{2}\,B_{p-2}(1/3)\pmod{p^{3}}.$$

(iii) For every prime $p>3$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}\frac{1}{(-192)^{k}}\binom{2k}{k}^{2}\binom{3k}{k} \;\equiv\;
\begin{cases}
x^{2}-2p \pmod{p^{2}} & \text{if } p\equiv 1\pmod{3} \text{ and } 4p=x^{2}+27y^{2} \text{ with } x,y\in\mathbb{Z},\\[4pt]
0 \pmod{p^{2}} & \text{if } p\equiv 2\pmod{3}.
\end{cases}$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search for proofs of this specific conjecture (the integrality of $a_n$ together with the supercongruences modulo $p^3$ and $p^2$ involving $\binom{2k}{k}^2\binom{3k}{k}/(-192)^k$) did not return a paper that explicitly establishes all three parts. Related conjectures of Z.-W. Sun about integrality of similar binomial polynomial sums and various supercongruences have been proved in the literature, but no source verifying this exact statement was located. Status is therefore unclear from available evidence.

status_evidence.title: Proof of Sun's conjectures on integer-valued polynomials (V. J. W. Guo)
status_evidence.snippet: Proves certain integer-valued-polynomial conjectures of Z.-W. Sun, but the conjecture stated above (with summand involving (5k+1) C(2k,k)^2 C(3k,k)/(-192)^k) is not among those treated.
status_evidence.claim: Related Sun conjectures on integrality have been proved, but this exact one is not found among them.

status_evidence.title: Proof of Sun's conjecture on the divisibility of certain binomial sums
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes integrality of a different family s_n involving central binomial coefficients of the form C(6k,3k)C(3k,k); does not treat the (-192)^k family.
status_evidence.claim: The cited proof addresses a different Sun conjecture, not the one in question.
